newsitem.title: ITALY: Rain in Italy's Lombardy region 60 pct below avge.
newsitem.headline: Rain in Italy's Lombardy region 60 pct below avge.

text.p: Rainfall this year in Italy's northern Lombardy region has been at least 60 percent below average, with drought and unseasonally high temperatures having a serious effect on crops, the Lombardy regional agricultural development agency (Ersal) said.

Ersal said in the period up to April drought mainly affected wheat and barley crops as well as hay for forage, while in the latest period the maize crop sown in April had been hit. But it was too soon to quantify the damage, an official said.
Average rainfall in the period January 1 to May 15 on the plain in Lombardy totalled just 100-150 millimetres against a normal average of 250-400 mm, Ersal said.
And even the occasional and sudden rainstorms seen in April and May, usually some of the wettest months of the year, had been nowhere near enough to relieve the problem.

"Basically, in the stratum of earth containing roots, to a depth of 1-1.5 metres, crops and vegetables in general have as yet only been able to find very limited water reserves and the situation looks like getting worse," said Luigi Mariani, head of Ersal's weather service.
Rainfall forecast up to the end of this week is again expected to be very scarce, he said.
Aggravating the situation are temperatures which in recent days have soared to over 30 degrees Celsius in Milan and surrounding areas.
Unless the trend reverses, the region's agriculture could very soon face serious water supply problems, Ersal said, urging frugality particularly with the "precious reserves" of the region's lakes.
To point up the unseasonal nature of the weather, Ersal noted that the last time rainfall in the region in the January-May 15 period had been so low was in 1976.
